title: See what you approve; scripts in their own thread
description: The approval dialog shows the script, after its first run a script can only load the files you approved, and scripts can no longer hang or close Voiden.

Added: The approval dialog shows the first lines of the script and has an "Open script" button, which opens it in the editor before you decide
Approvals now also cover every file a script loads with require() outside its folder: helpers elsewhere in the project and packages in node_modules. They join the approval on the script's first run

From then on, every file is checked against the approval at the moment the script loads it. A changed file, or a different file taking an approved one's place, stops the script before that file runs, and you're asked about it by name
When asked again, the dialog lists the files that changed
Changed: Each script runs in its own worker thread. A script that hangs is really stopped after 60 seconds, and process.exit() or a crash in a script no longer affects Voiden
Scripts must be in a folder (such as .voiden-auth/), not directly in the project root
Symbolic links in a script's folder are part of the approval
You'll be asked once to allow each script again after updating: approvals are stored in a new format
Fixed: A script folder with too many files gives advice instead of a bare error
Services sharing one script no longer open one approval dialog each
A folder whose name starts with two dots is no longer taken for a path outside the project

title: Network settings and clearer errors
description: auth.send now uses the same network settings as Voiden's own requests, and failures explain themselves.

Added: auth.send follows Voiden's "Disable TLS verification" setting and active proxy (with excluded domains)
Errors name any {{variables}} that aren't set in the active environment
A failing script's last auth.log lines are included in the error
Clear errors for options written in Postman's pm.sendRequest format (header, body objects)
Fixed: Network errors show the real cause (certificate, DNS, refused connection) instead of "fetch failed"

title: Initial release
description: First public release of Auto Auth.

Added: Auth config (.voiden-auth/auth.yaml) mapping APIs to auth scripts by URL prefix and/or folder
Auth scripts run in Node.js, with require() for helper files, project packages and Node modules, and an auth.send() helper with {{variable}} support
Approval before a script runs, repeated whenever the script or a file next to it changes; enforced in the main process
Headers cached per project, environment and service until expiry (read from JWTs automatically), with one shared login for parallel requests
Status bar item following the open request, with every service's token state on hover
Commands: Create example config, Clear cached tokens, Forget allowed scripts
